anomalies.observed: R43 is a 75R 100V thin-film resistor in the high-voltage cell-sense divider chain (R41 to R44 with C42 to C45 and C43). Its description and tolerance field read ±10%, while the three sibling resistors R41, R42 and R44 use the same MPN family and are described as ±0.1%.
anomalies.expected: Every resistor in this precision divider chain should carry the same ±0.1% tolerance as its siblings, so the per-cell voltage sense ratios stay matched.
anomalies.impact: A 10% element in the chain skews the divider ratio for that cell. The cell-voltage reading and any balancing decision based on it become inaccurate.

anomalies.observed: R36 is valued '24k' in the schematic, but its description and MPN both specify 24Ω (FRC0805J240TSD, '24Ω'). Its footprint and rating are 0805, 125mW.
anomalies.expected: A 24Ω part across VOUTN and VOUTP, as described by its MPN and description. A 24kΩ value would be a different bleed or sense element.
anomalies.impact: If the part is really 24Ω, it is a load across the output that would draw far more current than a 125mW 0805 can dissipate. If it is really 24kΩ, the BOM and description are wrong and the part is mis-sourced.

anomalies.observed: D30 pin 4 (A2, the anode of the second LED) is on ESTOP_OUT. R60 pin 2 is also on ESTOP_OUT, and R60 pin 1 feeds the cathode K2 (pin 2). Both ends of the second LED therefore sit on the same net, so no voltage can appear across it.
anomalies.expected: The second LED's anode should be on a driven rail, such as the switched 3.3V net used by its sibling LED1 (A1 on /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV), with its cathode current-limited through R60 to ESTOP_OUT.
anomalies.impact: The second indicator LED in the dual LED cannot light, so the e-stop status indication it provides is lost.

parsed.summary: The strongest deviation is R43, a ±10% resistor in the otherwise ±0.1% high-voltage cell-sense divider. R36 is also inconsistent: its value is 24k while its MPN and description say 24Ω. A third, lower-confidence finding is that D30's second LED has both ends on ESTOP_OUT.
